title: Dawn over Barovia
summary: Strahd von Zarovich is destroyed, and the sun rises over his valley.

epilogue.title: Barovia
epilogue.text: The mists thin through the summer and are gone by the harvest. For the first time in centuries, the road out of the valley leads somewhere.

epilogue.title: The Road Out
epilogue.text: The way home is open. Whether you take it at once, or stay to see what a Barovian summer looks like, is yours to decide.

epilogue.title: Ireena Kolyana
epilogue.text: At the pool, Ireena chose her own life. Now she gets to live it, and she never once looks up at the castle.

epilogue.title: Ireena Kolyana
epilogue.text: Ireena walks out of the castle's shadow into a morning that belongs to her. For the first time she can remember, nobody is watching her sleep.

epilogue.title: Ireena Kolyana
epilogue.text: Behind Krezk's wall, Ireena hears the bells before she hears the news. She is the first one through the gate to see the sun.

epilogue.title: Ireena Kolyana
epilogue.text: Wherever Ireena is when the sun comes up, she is free of him. It takes her a long time to believe it.

epilogue.title: Ismark
epilogue.text: Ismark goes home and takes up his father's chain of office. Nobody calls him the Lesser any more, and he never has to ask them to stop.

epilogue.title: The House on the Corner
epilogue.text: The old house at the village's edge stands quiet. Children play in its street again, and none of them are made of smoke.

epilogue.title: The House on the Corner
epilogue.text: The altar under the old house keeps the name of the one you left there. The house never asks for another.

epilogue.title: Vallaki
epilogue.text: The Baron declares a festival for the sun, and for once every soul in Vallaki comes without being made to.

epilogue.title: Vallaki
epilogue.text: With her master gone, Lady Wachter's hold on Vallaki crumbles within a week. The town decides it can manage without lords of any kind.

epilogue.title: Vallaki
epilogue.text: Father Lucian and Urwin Martikov hold Vallaki's council in the open square now, by daylight. The meetings are long, loud and entirely free.

epilogue.title: Vallaki
epilogue.text: Vallaki's gates stand open at noon for the first time in living memory. Nobody remembers who gave the order.

epilogue.title: The Wizard of Wines
epilogue.text: Davian and Adrian work the press side by side. The first vintage under a real sun is the best the family has ever made, and Davian says so.

epilogue.title: The Wizard of Wines
epilogue.text: Wine flows from the Martikov vineyard again, and under a real sun the grapes taste of something other than patience.

epilogue.title: The Keepers of the Feather
epilogue.text: The ravens of the Keepers of the Feather fly over the valley in daylight, with nobody left to spy on.

epilogue.title: Krezk
epilogue.text: The Abbot is found on the mountain road, kneeling toward the sunrise. Whatever judgment he walked out to meet, the light seems to have given it.

epilogue.title: Krezk
epilogue.text: In the abbey church the Abbot still sits where you left him. When the sun reaches his face he weeps, and does not stop for a long time.

epilogue.title: Krezk
epilogue.text: The bride the Abbot stitched together waits in the castle for a groom who will never come. Krezk's priests pray for her anyway.

epilogue.title: Krezk
epilogue.text: Krezk keeps its wall out of habit, but the gate stands open. Dmitri Krezkov greets every traveller himself.

epilogue.title: Ilya Krezkov
epilogue.text: Ilya Krezkov grows up to be taller than his father and twice as stubborn. Anna says that is the healing's fault.

epilogue.title: Ilya Krezkov
epilogue.text: Ilya never grows strong, but he grows. He spends his summers in the sun by the pool, which is more than any Krezkov child has had in a long while.

epilogue.title: Ilya Krezkov
epilogue.text: Ilya Krezkov does not see the spring. His parents bury him in sunlight, and find that it helps a little.

epilogue.title: Argynvostholt
epilogue.text: The beacon still burns on its hill, though the knights have laid down their swords at last. The dragon's light keeps watch alone.

epilogue.title: Argynvostholt
epilogue.text: The knights who rode with you to the castle ride home again. In the morning there are no knights at all, only armour resting in the mansion's hall.

epilogue.title: Argynvostholt
epilogue.text: The oath Vladimir made you swear is broken, and his knights know it. They lay down their arms in fury, and then, slowly, in relief.

epilogue.title: The Amber Temple
epilogue.text: High in the mountains the amber stays sealed. The voices inside it whisper to no one.

epilogue.title: The Gifts You Took
epilogue.text: The gifts you took from the amber did not die with their old customer. In quiet hours, they still ask to be used.

epilogue.title: Kasimir Velikov
epilogue.text: Kasimir gave all his years but one to bring Patrina back. He spends the last one at her side, and she spends it learning to forgive him.

epilogue.title: Kasimir Velikov
epilogue.text: Kasimir said at last what he owed his sister, and she let him go. He leaves Barovia lighter than he came.

epilogue.title: Patrina Velikovna
epilogue.text: Patrina's bones lie quiet in the crypts beneath the castle. Kasimir visits them once, alone, and never says what he told her.

epilogue.title: Rudolph van Richten
epilogue.text: Van Richten and Ezmerelda leave the valley together, already arguing about where the next monster is. Neither of them means to retire.

epilogue.title: Rudolph van Richten
epilogue.text: Van Richten packs away his disguises and his notes. He has one fewer monster to hunt, and admits he will not miss this one.

epilogue.title: Ezmerelda d'Avenir
epilogue.text: Ezmerelda's wagon is the first out of Barovia when the mists lift. She promises to come back. You both know she is lying.

epilogue.title: Mordenkainen
epilogue.text: Mordenkainen, his mind his own again, vanishes from his mountain one morning. He leaves a note of thanks that is slightly too pleased with itself.

epilogue.title: The Mad Mage
epilogue.text: The mad wizard of Mount Baratok still mutters on his peak, but he mutters toward the sun now.

epilogue.title: The Werewolves
epilogue.text: Emil's pack keeps to the high hills and hunts deer, not travellers. On full moons the villages bar their doors anyway, and Emil does not blame them.

epilogue.title: The Werewolves
epilogue.text: Kiril's pack has lost its master's leash but not its appetite. The roads are safer by day, and no safer by night.

epilogue.title: The Werewolves
epilogue.text: The den by the lake stands empty. The howling in the hills is only wolves now.

epilogue.title: Berez
epilogue.text: Berez sinks a little further into its marsh each spring. Nothing lives in the witch's hut now, and nothing wants to.

epilogue.title: Berez
epilogue.text: Baba Lysaga outlives the child she raised, and has no idea what to do with the time. She sits in the mud of Berez and waits for orders that never come.

epilogue.title: Old Bonegrinder
epilogue.text: The windmill on the hill grinds only grain now. The valley's children slowly stop having nightmares about pies.

epilogue.title: Old Bonegrinder
epilogue.text: One hag still keeps the mill on the hill. With the castle empty, she is suddenly the worst thing in the valley, and she knows it.

epilogue.title: Old Bonegrinder
epilogue.text: The coven still bakes on the hill. Sunlight has not improved the smell.
